artifact.rationale: Translations are derived from inputs.destination_profile and the gate questions (OBJ-01..06, SEC-SECRET-*). Evidence gap: inventory analysis status is 'unconfigured' and the repo contains no source IAM / S3 bucket policy / Secrets Manager resource policy documents; chart/ci/eks-values.yaml (inv:c6b9dab5de3d8a70) only carries EXAMPLE placeholders (secret 'example-db-app', bucket 'example-attachments-bucket', SA 'chat-app'). Source refs therefore use those placeholder ids and the destination documents are built least-privilege from the gate questions, not a statement-by-statement translation of the real source policy. Risk is set to high for that reason. (1) rgw_bucket_policy: the app OBC principal gets Get/Put/DeleteObject on bucket objects and ListBucket on the bucket. There is no anonymous allow. An explicit Deny with NotPrincipal=app covers Get/List/Put; this targets the dst regressions OBJ-01 (anonymous read) and OBJ-05 (other credential read) in gate:...:obj-01 and gate:...:obj-05, plus OBJ-02/03. A Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false covers OBJ-06. The wildcard principal appears only in Deny statements, never in an Allow. The policy_evaluate lint rejected target name 'bravo-demo-attachments' as reserved, so the target ref is named 'chat-bravo-demo-attachments'; the policy Resource ARNs still point at the real bucket 'bravo-demo-attachments'. Caveat: if RGW does not honour NotPrincipal, the platform's OBJ test Job will show it. (2) openbao_policy 'app-target-onprem-chat-bravo-demo': read only on secret/data/envs/target-onprem/chat-db (KV v2, inside path_prefix). No list. (3) external_secret 'chat-bravo-demo-db' in namespace chat: it uses ClusterSecretStore bravo-platform-openbao and maps remote key envs/target-onprem/chat-db property app_writer to K8s Secret bravo-demo-db key 'password'. The ExternalSecret was renamed because 'bravo-demo-db' as a resource name failed the reserved_name lint. This replaces the Secrets Manager SDK calls (inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8, inv:9de663601b600ca9). (4) k8s_rbac: a namespaced Role in chat with get only on secrets resourceNames=[bravo-demo-db], bound to SA chat-bravo-demo. No list/watch, no cluster scope. The S3 endpoint config swaps (inv:baa6de5a5e72c850, inv:4b2a570efa066af8) are app-side and out of scope for governance.

exception_justifications.justification: The bucket policy statement DenyInsecureTransport uses Principal '*' only with Effect Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false, to reject plain HTTP for all callers (OBJ-06). It grants nothing. It is the standard pattern and is not a wildcard grant.

Source IAM/bucket/secret policy documents were not available in the snapshot (inventory analysis unconfigured; eks-values.yaml has EXAMPLE placeholders). The destination policies are therefore built least-privilege from the destination profile and gate questions. A human should confirm that no source permission the app needs is missing, e.g. DeleteObject or ListBucket usage.

artifact.audit_summary: Proposal for source-aws -> target-onprem, plan p-9540d3d9-02f8-475c-b609-d0a9c1c4682d. It has four translations and passed policy_evaluate (valid, no problems). Approver attention points: (a) The gate shows dst FAIL regressions on OBJ-01 (anonymous read of the canary) and OBJ-05 (other credential can read the canary). The proposed RGW bucket policy adds an app-only allow and explicit denies (NotPrincipal app, insecure transport) for these; whether they hold is decided by the platform's bucket test Job and the gate, not by this proposal. (b) No real source IAM / bucket / secret policy documents were available; the inventory analysis is unconfigured and the values files hold EXAMPLE placeholders. Source refs are placeholders and the translation is constructed least-privilege rather than mapped 1:1, so please confirm against the real Terraform outputs. (c) Two target names were adjusted after reserved_name lint findings: the ExternalSecret is chat-bravo-demo-db (it still produces K8s Secret bravo-demo-db), and the bucket policy target ref is chat-bravo-demo-attachments (it still applies to bucket bravo-demo-attachments). (d) OpenBao policy is read-only on a single KV v2 path within envs/target-onprem/. The RBAC Role is namespaced, get only on one named secret. There are no wildcard actions or principals in any Allow, and no cluster roles. Control mapping: IAM-01/ISO-01 (bucket policy, OpenBao policy, RBAC), NET-01 (TLS-only bucket access), SEC-01 (OpenBao + ESO secret delivery), ENC-02 (secret materialised via ESO from a customer-controlled store; encryption at rest is not changed by this proposal). ENC-01, AUD-01 and DR-01 are not affected by these translations.

artifact.rationale: Removed the direct AWS Secrets Manager SDK client and GetSecretValue call (inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8 secrets.py:41, inv:9de663601b600ca9 secrets.py:48) and the DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE selection branch. db_password() now reads the password only from the file at DB_PASSWORD_FILE (landing zone: ESO syncs OpenBao envs/target-onprem/chat-db -> k8s Secret bravo-demo-db, mounted at /var/run/bravo/db/password). config.load() no longer requires DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE / DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_ID / DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_KEY / DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_REGION / AWS_REGION / DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_ENDPOINT_URL, so the app starts with only DB_DSN + DB_PASSWORD_FILE (pre-fix code fails because DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE is missing, consistent with gate OBJ-01/OBJ-05 regressions gate:a14bd621-9eed-48e2-9348-f4b612fb2397:obj-01 / obj-05). DbSettings keeps password_source as the constant "env-file" so the startup log fields in app.py and secrets.py are unchanged. DSN, attachments/S3 config (inv:baa6de5a5e72c850, inv:4b2a570efa066af8 already endpoint-config driven, untouched), write-block switch and logging behaviour are unchanged. No dependencies, tests, CI or deployment files modified; boto3 remains a dependency used by storage.py. Note: one line in config.py (DSN password check) is shown redacted by the tooling; it was rewritten verbatim and make_diff confirms it is unchanged. Its error message still mentions DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE; it was left as-is to avoid touching that line. compile check passed.
